History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
- 45-year-old woman with systemic lupus erythematosus (on methotrexate) presents with one-day history of right-sided pleuritic chest/back pain, shortness of breath, subjective fever, and two episodes of hemoptysis; clinician suspects chest infection/pneumonia and arranged same-day face-to-face review.

History:
- Presenting complaints: “breathless,” pleuritic pain in right posterior chest/back on deep inspiration, two episodes of blood-streaked sputum, subjective fever.
- Onset & timeline:
  • Fatigue, reduced exercise tolerance, and awareness of heartbeat for “a couple of weeks.”  
  • Acute escalation today – new pleuritic pain, dyspnea, low-grade fever, hemoptysis.
- Progression: Sudden onset today; no prior similar episodes reported.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: Pain triggered by deep breath; no relieving factors noted.
- Associated symptoms: Palpitations (sensation only), fatigue, no report of leg swelling, calf pain, or long-haul travel.
- Pertinent negatives: No long-haul flights; no personal/family history of venous thromboembolism; denies smoking.
- Review of systems otherwise not detailed.

Past Medical History:
- Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) – on immunosuppressive therapy.
  • Complications not discussed.
- No other chronic illnesses reported.

Medications:
- Methotrexate – dose/route/frequency not documented (taken this morning).

Allergies:
- No known drug allergies.
- No other allergies reported.

Social History:
- Occupation: Office/desk job.
- Living situation: Lives alone in a flat; has a pet cat.
- Tobacco: Non-smoker.
- Alcohol/substance use: Not discussed.
- Recent travel: No long-haul flights.

Family History:
- No family history of blood clots; no other familial illnesses mentioned.

Physical Examination:
(Virtual, limited)
- Pulse (patient-assisted radial count): 11–12 beats/10 s ≈ 66–72 bpm, regular.
- Capillary refill: Normal.
- Oropharynx: Visualized; no abnormal findings reported.
- Cervical lymph nodes: Patient palpated; no enlargement felt.
- Other vitals (BP, respiratory rate, temperature, SpO₂): Not obtained.
- No direct chest auscultation possible.

Investigations:
- None performed during teleconsultation.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Possible chest infection / pneumonia with pleuritic pain and hemoptysis.
  - Plan:
    • Arrange same-day face-to-face GP appointment for full examination (lung auscultation, BP, repeat pulse, temperature).
    • Consider empirical antibiotic therapy after in-person assessment.
    • Safety-net advice: seek urgent care if worsening breathlessness, massive hemoptysis, high fever, or feeling acutely unwell.

Issue 2: Immunosuppression due to SLE and methotrexate.
  - Plan:
    • Highlight to reviewing clinician—lower threshold for investigations, hospital referral if infection confirmed.
    • Ensure routine SLE/methotrexate monitoring up to date (not addressed today).

Issue 3: Patient anxiety about possible lung cancer.
  - Plan:
    • Reassured that acute presentation more suggestive of infection than malignancy.
    • If symptoms persist or imaging indicated, arrange chest X-ray to rule out malignancy or other pathology.

General plan items:
- Support team number provided; patient to call for booking same-day review.
- No prescriptions issued pending physical assessment.
- Follow-up arrangements to be determined after in-person evaluation.

Quality checks:

• Missing/expected elements:
  – Complete vital signs (BP, RR, Temp, SpO₂).  
  – Detailed drug list (dose, route, frequency of methotrexate; other medications if any).  
  – Formal allergy documentation beyond “none.”  
  – Alcohol history, immunization status.

• Internal conflicts:
  – Patient’s name given as “Tracy Chapman” at start; later responds “Doris” when doctor forgets (conflict noted).

• Transcript quality:
  – Generally clear; occasional conversational overlaps and minor inaudible phrases but core clinical content understandable.
